topics.t: Delimitation package: the freeze on States’ Lok Sabha share to be extended to 2051
topics.news: The Centre has proposed, in the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Bill, 2026, to extend the freeze on the readjustment of Lok Sabha seats among States until the year 2051. Article 82 now says that until the figures of the first Census taken after 2026 are published, it shall not be necessary to readjust the allocation of seats; the Bill replaces this with “until the year 2051”. The reference to the 1971 Census is dropped, and the distribution among States is to follow Article 334A, while constituency boundaries inside a State will use the latest published Census figures on the date the Amendment comes into force.

rows: Present Article 82

Readjustment of seats after each Census, but the allocation among States stays frozen until the first Census after 2026 is published; the 1971 population is used among States and the 2001 Census inside States.
Proposed sunset
The freeze is extended until the year 2051, about 25 years longer than at present.
1971 reference
The Bill drops the reference to the 1971 Census for the distribution among States, which is to be determined in accordance with Article 334A.
Constituency boundaries
Boundaries of individual constituencies within a State will be fixed on the latest published Census figures available when the Amendment begins.
Size of the House
The package raises the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 seats and brings the one-third reservation for women into force after delimitation.

ul: **Why it matters:** the allocation of seats among States touches the balance between “one person, one vote” and federalism, since States that stabilised their population earlier would lose weight if seats followed the latest Census.
**Way forward:** agreement among parties on the seat formula and timing, and detailed examination of the Bills by a parliamentary committee, would help build confidence.

prel.d: Fixing the number of seats and the boundaries of territorial constituencies, done by a Delimitation Commission whose orders have the force of law.
A provision that makes a rule lapse on a stated date or event unless it is extended.

qs.q: Examine the federal concerns raised by delimitation. Is extending the freeze on seat allocation among States a sufficient safeguard?

topics.t: Delimitation politics: the Cabinet package and the stand of Tamil Nadu parties
topics.news: The Union Cabinet has approved a legislative package on delimitation that is to be introduced at the special sitting of Parliament on Monday. The DMK, which opposed the April 2026 proposal based on the 2011 Census, has laid down two conditions for support: a longer sunset clause on the freeze, and a legal guarantee that the existing ratio of parliamentary and Assembly constituencies among States, based on the 1971 Census, continues unchanged. The package addresses both demands.

rows: April 2026 proposal

An earlier Constitution amendment based on the 2011 Census would have raised seats and was criticised for disadvantaging States with slower population growth; it did not get the special majority in the Lok Sabha.
Tamil Nadu’s stand
A resolution of the Tamil Nadu Assembly in February 2024 and a Joint Action Committee meeting in Chennai in March 2025 opposed delimitation on the basis of the post-2026 Census.
Concern of the South
Even if the proportion of seats is kept, a larger House raises the absolute numbers of the northern States, and the redrawing of boundaries could affect electoral outcomes.
Special majority
A Constitution amendment needs a majority of the total membership of each House and two-thirds of the members present and voting.

ul: **Why it matters:** it shows how a Constitution amendment depends on building consensus across regional and national parties.
**Way forward:** protecting the share of each State while expanding the House needs transparent criteria and the involvement of States.

prel.d: Under Article 368, a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting in each House.
A coalition of parties and groups formed to press a common demand on an issue.

qs.q: Discuss the role of regional parties in shaping decisions on delimitation and women’s reservation.

topics.t: Vindhyagiri, the last of the Nilgiri-class stealth frigates, handed over to the Navy
topics.news: The Indian Navy received Vindhyagiri, the seventh and final ship of the Nilgiri-class (Project 17A) stealth frigates, from Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Ltd. in Kolkata. All seven ships have now been delivered within 23 months of the first ship, INS Nilgiri, handed over on 20 December 2024. The Defence Ministry said the milestone completes the Project 17A delivery programme.

rows: Design and oversight
Designed by the Navy’s Warship Design Bureau and overseen by the Warship Overseeing Team in Kolkata.
Propulsion
Combined Diesel or Gas (CODOG) system, with a diesel engine and a gas turbine, and an Integrated Platform Management System.
Role
Multi-mission frigates with weapons and sensors for anti-surface, anti-air and anti-submarine warfare.
Indigenous content
About 75 per cent, with more than 200 micro, small and medium enterprises involved.
Employment
About 4,000 people directly and over 10,000 indirectly.

ul: **Why it matters:** it strengthens indigenous warship design and the defence industrial base under the self-reliance push.
**Way forward:** reducing dependence on imported engines and weapon systems is the next step.

prel.d: A warship designed to reduce its radar, infrared and acoustic signature.
A propulsion arrangement in which a diesel engine drives the ship at cruising speed and a gas turbine is used for high speed.

qs.q: Discuss the significance of Project 17A for indigenous warship building. What challenges remain in achieving self-reliance in naval equipment?

topics.t: Uttarakhand to treat accidental fires in homes as disasters
topics.news: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami announced that accidental fires in residential buildings will now be classified as disasters, and affected families will receive relief in line with State Disaster Response Fund norms. The announcement follows a fire in the remote village of Pawani in Mori tehsil of Uttarkashi district that engulfed 39 houses and affected 56 families. Each affected family has been promised financial aid of Rs 5 lakh.

rows: State Disaster Response Fund
Constituted by each State under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, for immediate relief; the Centre contributes a share of the funds.
Notified disasters
Relief norms apply to calamities notified for the fund, and fire is among them.
Local disasters
States may also treat a locally frequent event as a State-specific disaster and use a limited part of the fund for relief.
Why hill villages suffer
Wooden houses built close together, narrow lanes and distance from fire stations raise losses.

ul: **Why it matters:** classifying such fires brings predictable relief for families who lose everything.
**Way forward:** fire-safe building practices, village fire kits and trained volunteers reduce the damage.

prel.d: The State Disaster Response Fund, used for immediate relief to people hit by notified disasters.
The State-level body under the Disaster Management Act, headed by the Chief Minister.

qs.q: How can disaster relief frameworks be made responsive to local hazards such as village fires in hill States?

topics.t: Telangana to issue pattadar passbooks with land maps
topics.news: Telangana has begun what is described as a first-of-its-kind exercise in the country: pattadar passbooks for farmers with an embedded map of each holding, including its coordinates. The passbook will carry a unique code, like a QR code, that can be scanned to see details of the land. It will be issued after the resurvey of 10,900 revenue villages, which is being taken up in phases, and will help build a comprehensive digital land registry.

rows: Pattadar passbook
A document that records the ownership of a landholding of a farmer in the revenue records.
What is new
A map of the land and its coordinates in the passbook, with a unique scannable code.
Survey
Resurvey of 10,900 revenue villages in phases, to be followed by issue of the new passbooks.
Centre’s scheme
The Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme promotes a 14-digit unique land parcel identification number for every parcel.
Constitutional position
Land and land revenue records are State subjects in the Seventh Schedule.

ul: **Why it matters:** clear maps and records reduce boundary disputes, speed up loans against land and make transactions simpler.
**Way forward:** linking survey, registration and mutation in one system keeps records current.

prel.d: The register that shows who owns or cultivates a plot of land.
A unique number for each plot, so that records, maps and transactions can be linked.

qs.q: How does digitisation of land records improve governance and farmers’ access to credit?

topics.t: Keralam Assembly session from 30 November: anti-ragging Bill on the agenda
topics.news: The third session of the 16th Keralam Legislative Assembly will begin on 30 November and run until 10 December. Nine Bills will be taken up, including an anti-ragging Bill named after J.S. Sidharthan, a 20-year-old student whose death caused a Statewide outcry over ragging. The Assembly will also consider a motion to withdraw the Kerala Private Universities (Establishment and Regulation) Bill, 2025, which was passed on 25 March 2025 when the previous LDF government was in power.

rows: Summoning
The Governor summons the House of the State Legislature to meet and prorogues it, under Article 174.
Ragging
The Supreme Court acted on ragging after the Raghavan Committee in 2007, and the UGC framed regulations on curbing ragging in higher educational institutions in 2009.
Private universities Bill
The 2025 Bill was passed in March 2025 under the previous government; the new Assembly will consider a motion to withdraw it.

ul: **Why it matters:** the session tests how States use their own laws to tackle campus safety and regulate higher education.
**Way forward:** strict enforcement, student helplines and accountability of institutions would give the law teeth.

prel.d: Ending a session of the legislature by order of the Governor, without dissolving the House.
UGC rules that make institutions responsible for preventing ragging and set penalties for offenders.

qs.q: What measures are needed to prevent ragging in educational institutions? Evaluate the role of legislation.

topics.t: MCD adds ten mechanical sweepers to curb Delhi’s road dust
topics.news: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta flagged off ten mechanical road sweepers at the Municipal Corporation of Delhi headquarters, taking the fleet to 76. They are the first of 70 large sweepers ordered; the remaining 60 are to be deployed by July-end, taking the fleet to 136 across the MCD’s 12 zones. Each machine can clean at least 40 lane-kilometres a shift, and the civic body plans to raise daily coverage from 2,100 to 5,000 lane-kilometres. The step comes as the ‘poor’ category of air continues in the capital, with an Air Quality Index of 231 on Friday.

rows: Road dust
A major source of particulate pollution in Delhi, especially in winter when winds are weak.
Air quality category
An AQI of 201 to 300 is ‘poor’; 301 to 400 is ‘very poor’; 401 and above is ‘severe’.
Regulator
The Commission for Air Quality Management in the National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas, set up by a 2021 law, coordinates action in the region.
Coverage
Planned rise in daily cleaning from 2,100 to 5,000 lane-kilometres.

ul: **Why it matters:** controlling dust is one of the cheapest and fastest ways to reduce PM10 and PM2.5 in winter.
**Way forward:** pairing sweepers with water sprinkling, paving of road edges and control of construction dust gives lasting results.

prel.d: Particles of 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter that can enter deep into the lungs.
A scale that converts pollutant levels into a single number and a category from ‘good’ to ‘severe’.

qs.q: Examine the causes of winter air pollution in Delhi and the effectiveness of mechanical road sweeping as a control measure.

topics.t: Delhi and Bihar sign pact to run buses on 18 inter-State routes
topics.news: Delhi and Bihar signed an agreement to run inter-State bus services on 18 routes connecting the national capital with 13 destinations in Bihar. The services were flagged off at the Maharana Pratap Inter-State Bus Terminal at Kashmere Gate. Each State has been allocated 12 permits for every route; the Bihar State Road Transport Corporation has procured 75 non-AC and 74 AC buses, while Delhi plans to run 150 buses under a public-private partnership model. Fares are expected to range from Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000 for non-sleeper and sleeper services.

rows: Legal basis
Inter-State road transport is arranged through permits and reciprocal agreements between State transport authorities under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Routes
Delhi to Araria, Bihar Sharif, Bhagalpur, Buxar, Darbhanga, East Champaran, Gaya, Kishanganj, Madhubani, Muzaffarpur, Nawada, Patna and Purnia.
Beneficiaries
About 20 lakh people from Bihar working and studying in Delhi are expected to benefit.
Model
Delhi’s fleet will be run on the public-private partnership model.

ul: **Why it matters:** reliable inter-State buses support the mobility of migrant workers and students.
**Way forward:** integrated ticketing, safety for women and real-time tracking would raise quality.

prel.d: An understanding between two States on the number of permits and routes each will operate.
A long-term arrangement in which a private operator provides a public service under a contract with the government.

qs.q: How do inter-State arrangements for road transport support labour mobility and cooperative federalism?

topics.t: Tamil Nadu announces 15 days of paternity leave for male government employees
topics.news: The Tamil Nadu government has announced 15 days of paternity leave for male government employees. The step recognises the father’s role in the care of a newborn and the recovering mother. Commentators have urged that such leave be extended to private-sector employees and that parental leave be made gender-neutral.

rows: Central rules
A male central government employee with fewer than two surviving children is entitled to 15 days of paternity leave around the birth of a child.
Maternity benefit
The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, as amended in 2017, provides 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
Private sector
There is no law that gives paternity leave to private-sector employees; some employers offer it as policy.
Social aim
Shared care work supports women’s participation in the workforce.

ul: **Why it matters:** paternity leave helps share unpaid care work and encourages fathers to take part in child rearing.
**Way forward:** a gender-neutral parental leave policy for all sectors would widen the benefit.

prel.d: Paid leave given to a father around the birth or adoption of a child.
Household and care tasks without pay, which fall mostly on women.

qs.q: Discuss the need for gender-neutral parental leave in India.

topics.t: Nepal’s Prime Minister visits India: a road map for the partnership
topics.news: Prime Minister Balendra Shah of Nepal made his first bilateral visit abroad to India, meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday, 23 November 2026. The two sides announced a road map titled “Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal”, with 10 pillars. The first three focus on developmental and economic ties, physical and digital connectivity, and energy and climate. The visit delivered long-pending support, including about 1.6 billion US dollars in grants and lines of credit, steps to improve air connectivity, new railway links and hydropower investment.

rows: Road map
“Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal”, a 10-pillar vision for the partnership.
Support
About 1.6 billion US dollars in grants and lines of credit, with moves on air connectivity, railways and hydropower.
Monitoring
The plan includes reviving a High-Level Monitoring Group to track progress.
Policy frame
India’s Neighbourhood First policy; the Treaty of Peace and Friendship of 1950 is the base of the relationship.

ul: **Why it matters:** Nepal is a land-linked neighbour with open borders, and its choices affect India’s security and economy.
**Way forward:** timely delivery of projects and direct communication channels at the leadership level will sustain trust.

prel.d: India’s policy of giving priority to relations with immediate neighbours.
A loan facility that India extends to another country for projects, often tied to Indian goods and services.

qs.q: Discuss the importance of Nepal in India’s Neighbourhood First policy. What are the challenges in delivering development partnership?

topics.t: Bangladesh calls Sheikh Hasina’s presence in India a ‘thorn’ in ties
topics.news: Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Humayun Kabir, said that the presence of the deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in India has become a “thorn” in bilateral ties and that New Delhi is beginning to realise the strain it causes. He said she could return only under the extradition treaty between the two countries and that India is in a difficult position as it can neither send her away nor avoid dealing with her presence.

rows: Extradition treaty
India and Bangladesh signed an extradition treaty in 2013, which was amended in 2016.
Background
Hasina left Bangladesh in August 2024 after a mass uprising and has stayed in India since.
Why it is hard
Extradition depends on the treaty’s conditions, including exceptions for political offences.
Wider ties
Trade, connectivity, water sharing and border management remain priorities for both sides.

ul: **Why it matters:** the issue is a test for India’s ties with a major neighbour and for its policy on political asylum.
**Way forward:** keeping economic cooperation going while handling the legal question through established channels.

prel.d: The surrender of a person accused or convicted of a crime by one country to another under a treaty or law.
A common clause that bars extradition when the offence is political in nature.

qs.q: Examine the challenges in India–Bangladesh relations after 2024 and suggest a way forward.

topics.t: Makkah defence alliance denounces Houthi attacks as the Yemen conflict flares
topics.news: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, the members of the Makkah Alliance for Defence, denounced continued attacks by Yemen’s Houthi (Ansar Allah) rebels and vowed to strengthen cooperation. Their top security officials and diplomats met in Islamabad after signing a NATO-style pact in August. The statement came a day after a Houthi attack on a Saudi oil refinery and a Saudi strike that killed 11 people in Yemen, as the Saudi-led coalition said it shot down a drone aimed at Riyadh.

rows: Members
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye; the pact was signed in August and is described as NATO-style.
Houthis
The Ansar Allah movement controls much of northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa, and fights the internationally recognised government.
Concern for India
Attacks on Gulf energy facilities affect oil prices and the safety of about nine million Indians living in the Gulf region.
Shipping
Instability around Yemen threatens sea lanes through the Red Sea and Bab-el-Mandeb.

ul: **Why it matters:** new security groupings in West Asia reshape alignments that matter for India’s energy and diaspora interests.
**Way forward:** India’s balanced engagement with Gulf States and support for peaceful settlement protects its interests.

prel.d: A Zaidi Shia armed movement in Yemen, officially called Ansar Allah.
The strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa that links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.

qs.q: Analyse the implications of new security groupings in West Asia for India’s interests.

topics.t: Strobe Talbott, who helped repair India–US ties after Pokhran-II, dies at 80
topics.news: Strobe Talbott, the former United States Deputy Secretary of State under President Bill Clinton, has died at the age of 80. He and the then External Affairs Minister Jaswant Singh held a series of talks that helped bridge the gap between the two countries after India’s nuclear tests at Pokhran in May 1998.

rows: Pokhran-II
India conducted nuclear tests on 11 and 13 May 1998 under Operation Shakti; the United States imposed sanctions.
The dialogue
The Talbott–Jaswant Singh talks covered non-proliferation, security and economic ties and prepared the ground for the later improvement in relations.
Visit
President Clinton visited India in March 2000, the first visit by a US President in over two decades.
Later ties
Relations deepened in the following years, including the 2008 civil nuclear agreement.

ul: **Why it matters:** the episode is a lesson in using sustained diplomacy to repair ties after a crisis.
**Way forward:** steady high-level engagement keeps the strategic partnership resilient to differences.

prel.d: Efforts to stop the spread of nuclear weapons and related technology.
The code name for India’s nuclear tests of May 1998.

qs.q: Discuss how diplomacy helped to repair India–US ties after the 1998 nuclear tests.

topics.t: Shenzhou-24 carries Pakistan’s first astronaut to China’s Tiangong station
topics.news: China launched the Shenzhou-24 mission on 25 November, taking Pakistan’s first astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, to the Tiangong space station. It is seen as part of Beijing’s “Space Silk Road”. Commentators note that Pakistan’s space cooperation with China contrasts with India’s access to facilities in the United States and Europe, and that science-based diplomacy could open space for India–Pakistan engagement on regional issues such as the environment.

rows: Tiangong
China’s modular space station in low Earth orbit, built after China was kept out of the International Space Station.
Pakistan’s agency
The Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) is Pakistan’s space agency.
Regional groupings
The Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organisation, led by China, includes Bangladesh among its members.
India’s programme
India is preparing its Gaganyaan crewed mission, and an Indian astronaut flew to the International Space Station on the Axiom-4 mission in 2025.

ul: **Why it matters:** space cooperation is becoming a tool of influence among neighbours.
**Way forward:** India can offer regional space cooperation through open platforms such as satellite and data sharing.

prel.d: The Chinese space station, meaning ‘Heavenly Palace’.
Pakistan’s national space agency.

qs.q: How is space becoming a new domain of geopolitical competition in South Asia?

topics.t: India’s place in the global energy order
topics.news: The International Energy Agency’s World Energy Outlook calls 2026 “a year of unprecedented disruption”, describing the Strait of Hormuz crisis as “the largest threat to energy security in history”. The strait carries nearly a fifth of the world’s maritime oil and gas. India is the world’s third-largest primary energy consumer, with a 6.1 per cent share, and its energy demand is projected to grow about 2.5 per cent a year through 2035, three times the global rate.

rows: Global mix, 2025
Fossil fuels were about 86.2 per cent of primary energy: oil 33.5, coal 27.7 and natural gas 25.1 per cent. Renewables supplied 5.9, nuclear 5.2 and hydro 2.7 per cent.
Electrification
Electricity is about 23 per cent of global final energy demand and is expected to reach 30 per cent by 2035.
Renewables
Their share of global electricity generation is expected to rise from about a third to half by 2035.
India’s dependence
India imports around 40 per cent of its energy, including about 90 per cent of its crude oil and 50 per cent of its natural gas.
India’s power mix
Renewable capacity has crossed half of installed capacity, but about 70 per cent of electricity is still generated from fossil fuels.
Per-capita use
India’s annual electricity use of 1,153 units per person is about a third of the global average.

ul: **Why it matters:** supply shocks from West Asia hit India through oil prices, the import bill and inflation.
**Way forward:** faster electrification, storage, efficiency and a diverse import basket advance the goal of energy independence by 2047.

prel.d: A narrow strait between Iran and Oman through which a large part of the world’s oil and gas moves.
Reliable and affordable access to energy at all times.

qs.q: Discuss the challenges to India’s energy security and the steps needed to reach energy independence by 2047.

topics.t: New Zealand’s coalition falls one seat short of a majority
topics.news: New Zealand’s final results for the 7 November election show the ruling centre-right coalition with 65 seats in the 130-seat Parliament, one short of a majority. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s National Party won 40 seats, ACT 13 and New Zealand First 12. Labour, the largest opposition party, won 36, and the new Opportunity Party won seven. Mr Luxon needs the support of the Opportunity Party to remain in power, and failing a deal the country would hold new elections.

rows: Electoral system
New Zealand uses mixed-member proportional representation, in which party votes decide each party’s share of seats.
Majority
In a House of 130, a majority requires 66 seats.
Seats won
National 40, Labour 36, ACT 13, New Zealand First 12, Opportunity 7.
Options
A coalition, or a confidence-and-supply agreement in which a party backs the government on key votes without joining it.

ul: **Why it matters:** the result shows how proportional systems produce coalition governments and make small parties important.
**Way forward:** a stable arrangement is needed to avoid a fresh election.

prel.d: A system that combines constituency seats with party-list seats so that the final seats match party vote shares.
An agreement in which a party supports the government on confidence votes and budgets without holding ministries.

qs.q: Compare proportional representation with the first-past-the-post system in terms of stability and representation.
